surfaces.part: pumice scatter (small scattered stones on ground)

answer.evidence: The object is a sparse scatter of a few small stone blobs (widths 2-8 px) spread across rows 4-12 with transparent gaps between them. It has no standing volume, no front-edge line, no eave shadow and no front face of 3+ rows. It reads as a flat decal seen from above, which matches the flat kind. Per the contract this is a top-down slab with no front face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny cluster of a few pixels, smaller than one 16x16 tile, on an empty dark background. It is not the 4x3-tile ground patch the brief asks for, so it does not match the reference kind. The measured facts give 0 visible tones per tile because the piece is under one tile, so I judged by eye. By eye it has only about 2-3 tones (8 distinct colours in total) against the references' 3-7 visible tones per tile with grain and tufts. Its dark edge pixels are 100% near-neutral, which reads as a grey/black sticker outline, while the grass reference is 0% neutral and carries tinted shading. There is no ground coverage, no tiling surface, and no grain or clump texture. It is far thinner and flatter than either reference.
